prompt_text: What is the best AI video ad maker?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” AI video ad maker — the right choice depends on what you need (realistic human presenters vs. fast templated social clips, budget, languages, editing control, repurposing long-form content, etc.). That said, these platforms are the most popular and high-quality options in different use cases:

Top picks (by use case)
- Realistic AI presenters / product demos
  - Synthesia — best for very realistic, multilingual AI presenters and polished explainer ads.
  - HeyGen (Movio/Elai family) — good alternative with strong avatars and voice options.
  - Pros: natural-looking presenters, many languages, easy script → video pipeline.
  - Cons: less control over custom visual effects; cost per seat or per video can add up.

- Fast social ads, templates, brand kit, collaboration
  - Canva (Video) — easiest, huge template library, brand kit, team features.
  - InVideo / Promo.com — strong social ad templates and stock assets.
  - Pros: fast, low learning curve, good value for teams producing many short ads.
  - Cons: less advanced AI presenter tech or cutting-edge generative visuals.

- Repurposing long-form into short ads / clips
  - Opus Clip, Pictory — automatically chop long videos into high-performing short clips.
  - Pros: saves editing time, automatic highlight selection/captions.
  - Cons: may need manual refinement for brand messaging.

- Advanced generative visuals / creative effects
  - Runway — best for AI-based editing, background removal, generative fill and novel effects.
  - Kaiber / Runway Gen models — useful if you want stylized visuals beyond templates.
  - Pros: highly creative outputs and fine-grained editing.
  - Cons: steeper learning curve and varying output control.

- Budget / entry-level
  - Canva free/Pro, Lumen5 — low-cost, easy to start with.
  - Pros: inexpensive, lots of ready-to-use assets.
  - Cons: limits on advanced AI features.

What to evaluate when choosing
- Primary goal (social ad, explainer, product demo, UGC-style)
- Need for human-like presenters or custom avatars
- Languages and voiceover quality
- Templates, brand kit, and team collaboration features
- Output formats, resolutions, and platform presets (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube)
- Analytics, A/B testing, and ad-platform integrations
- Pricing model (per-video, seat subscription, credits)
- IP/voice licensing and usage rights
- Trial availability and speed of turnaround

Pricing note
- Prices vary widely and change often; most vendors offer free trials or low-cost starter plans — try 2–3 candidates with a real brief to compare.

If you tell me:
- your budget,
- the ad format/length/platform (e.g., 15s TikTok, 30s Facebook, 60s YouTube),
- whether you need an AI presenter or just templated creative,
I’ll recommend 1–2 best options and a quick evaluation checklist you can use on their free trials.
